Priya (PM): Quick sync — dropping the PRD fragment for Dedicated Capacity SLA + autoscale sizing. Need sign-off on acceptance criteria and edge cases. pinging @Luca @Jordan @Sam
Luca (Eng): on it. quick Q: are we using p95 or p99 for customer-facing SLA?
Priya (PM): proposing p95 for public SLA, p99 internal target for alerting. customer contracts expect p95 guarantees.
Jordan (ML): add note about quantization variance and eval guardrails. we should require runbook for any model fallback that changes token-level outputs.
Sam (SRE): also need concrete load test thresholds and circuit-breaker behavior. without those autoscale triggers are vague.
Ava (Solutions): enterprise pilot asked for burst window of 5m guaranteed capacity. need to map to reserved GPU counts or burst pool policy.
Priya (PM): here's the acceptance snippet I drafted — please flag anything missing:
```
Acceptance criteria:
- SLA: p95 latency <= 120ms for short responses (<=128 tokens) under committed throughput
- Internal target: p99 latency <= 450ms
- Throughput sizing: baseline per-GPU sustained throughput = 2k tokens/sec (quantized model)
- Autoscale policy: add 1 GPU when queue depth > 200 requests OR GPU util > 70% for 120s
- Scale-down: remove 1 GPU when util < 30% for 180s and queue depth < 50
- Fallbacks: automatic routing to hosted compatible model within same region if capacity unavailable
- Observability: per-route token/latency SLI, and per-deploy regression alerts tied to eval suites
```
Luca (Eng): looks good. recommend replacing absolute queue depth with proportional queue per-GPU in final PRD (e.g., queue_per_gpu > 200). avoids weirdness as pool size changes.
Sam (SRE): re: scale down — add a safety cooldown (10m) after any scale up to avoid flip-flop. also capture cold-start tail behavior as an edge case.
Jordan (ML): quantitative test plan: include regression threshold of 1% KL divergence on key eval prompts when switching to quantized variant. If exceeded -> block automatic rollout.
Ava (Solutions): add an acceptance item: documented customer-facing degraded-mode behavior and SLA credit computation for bursts > committed capacity. customers will ask.
Priya (PM): good catches. will update: - change queue threshold to per-gpu basis - add 10m cooldown - include KL divergence check - add burst penalty doc.
DeployBot: deploy checklist item created: "dedicated-sla-prd-review-v1" assigned to Priya (PM), Luca (Eng), Sam (SRE)
Luca (Eng): edge cases I'd call out explicitly:
- noisy neighbor with single tenant oversubscription (pinned vs shared pools)
- KV-cache warmup: first 30s after model load shows degraded throughput
- partial failure: 1 GPU OOM during spool -> should gracefully retry on different instance and bump _error-rate_ gauge
- multi-model routing: ensure routing keys maintain model affinity to avoid cold KV cache thrash
Sam (SRE): agreed. also simulate regional failover: ensure fallback to hosted variant adds <200ms routing overhead in our tests.
Jordan (ML): add a preflight acceptance: any model added to Dedicated must pass quantization smoke & eval (latency + quality gate) in staging before rollout.
Ava (Solutions): customer ask: deterministic billing footprint for reserved pools during burst. we'll need precise formula in PRD (committed + burst_capacity * time).
Priya (PM): next steps: I'll incorporate edits and upload updated PRD before Tue sync. If nobody objects by EOD tomorrow I will lock acceptance criteria and kick off load test plan with Sam.
Luca (Eng): +1 from eng
Jordan (ML): +1 from ML
Sam (SRE): +1 from SRE
Ava (Solutions): +1 from solutions
Priya (PM): thanks all — linking this thread into the PRD doc and tagging reviewers when I push changes.
